Okay. Thank you, Chair. The subject property is addressed as 808-836
Corlin Avenue East. The property is located on the east side of Corlin Avenue East,
immediately south of the Highway 78 on Rand.
The property has an area of approximately 1.3 hectares
and a frontage of 114 meters on Portland.
The property contains three existing buildings.
The surrounded lands contain a wide range of land uses
of various heights and densities, and the property backs on to two apartment buildings
that have frontage on Van Yen Drive.
The subject property is within a protected Major Transit Station Area or PMTSA, as outlined
on maps two and four of the Official Plan.
Property is located approximately 660 metres from the Block Line Island Station stop and
is currently split designated on map three of the Official Plan as commercial and general
industrial employment.
A small portion of the lands is designated natural heritage conservation due to the Schneider Creek floodplain.
The property was excluded from the Growing Together East study since the subject of Official Plan Amendment, or OPA,
and Zoning By-law Amendment, or ZVA, applications had already been submitted and were already under review.
The applicant is requesting an OPA and ZVA to facilitate redevelopment of the property with a high-rise mixed-use development.
The OPA would change the land use designation of the developable portions of the property to strategic growth area C.
The developable portions of the subject property are currently split zoned under zoning bylaw 85.1
as arterial commercial zone and general industrial zone with site-specific provisions.

To facilitate the proposed development concept, the applicant has requested a ZBA to change the zoning of the developable portions of the subject property to Strategic Growth Area 4 Zone, or SGA 4, with a site-specific provision and a holding provision under Bylaw 2019-051.
So, change in Bylaw.
In addition, the ZVA would change the small portions of the property that are not
developable due to the floodplain to natural conservation zone or a NHC1.
The holding provision would ensure that no new sensitive land uses are permitted until
such time as a detailed noise study is conducted and implementation measures have been addressed
and a record of site condition has been completed.
The proposed development concept comprises a mixed-use development containing three high-rise
residential towers, 22, 27, and 30 stories in height, situated on a shared six-story
podium.
A total of 977 dwelling units are proposed, consisting of one, two, and three-bedroom
units.
And the ground floor of the podium would contain a total of 532 square meters of commercial
use.
Various amenities and shared common areas would be provided throughout the development.
Most parking would be included within the podium structure, which would be wrapped with active
use along Cortland Avenue and within one level of underground parking.
Bicycle parking would be provided in accordance with the requested zoning.
Access would be achieved by a single driveway leading to Cortland, which would be shared
for the neighboring property to the south
and located as far away as possible
